name: Arcarine

lead: Arcarine (ORM-11984) is a selective androgen receptor modulator that Orion Corporation developed for conditions such as benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis.
It reached Phase I trials before development was discontinued. It is not a marketed product, and no human data on muscle or appearance outcomes have been published.

paras: As a SARM, it was designed to activate androgen receptors in tissues like muscle and bone while having weaker effects on the prostate. Its structure was never disclosed, and a rat study of local delivery reported it did not act as an anabolic agent in that model.
No safety data are published. SARMs as a class are unapproved, banned by WADA, and have been linked in case reports to liver injury with recreational use.

lead: Arcarine (development code ORM-11984) is an investigational selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed by the Finnish company Orion Corporation. SARMs are drugs designed to activate the androgen receptor in some tissues, such as muscle and bone, more than in others, such as the prostate [1][2].

Arcarine was studied for benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis. It reached Phase I clinical trials, after which development was discontinued, and its chemical structure has not been disclosed [1][2]. Published information is sparse, and no trial results for appearance or muscle-building use are available.

paras: Orion Corporation developed Arcarine as a candidate for benign prostatic hyperplasia, hypogonadism and osteoporosis [2]. Wikipedia's SARM article lists it among candidates that reached Phase I and were then discontinued, with an undisclosed structure [1]. The reasons for discontinuation are not stated in the sources reviewed.

One study cited on Wikipedia tested local delivery of the compound in a rat bone-marrow ablation model and reported that it failed as an anabolic agent in that setting [2]. The wider SARM class has produced mixed human results: Phase III testing of enobosarm increased lean body mass without significantly improving physical function, and no SARM had been approved by the FDA or EMA as of 2023 [1].

WADA has prohibited SARMs as a class since 2008, and many products sold online as SARMs have been found mislabeled in at least one study [1]. Arcarine itself is not described as a gray-market product in the sources reviewed.
No studies found. Arcarine reached Phase I only, and no human results have been published in the sources reviewed [1][2].
